pipelines-backpressure-buffer-ownership.title: Handle PipeReader buffers with explicit consumption and backpressure
pipelines-backpressure-buffer-ownership.short: Sequence parsing is tied to buffer ownership
pipelines-backpressure-buffer-ownership.summary: System.IO.Pipelines separates reading from consumption so high-throughput parsers can process segmented buffers without copying every chunk.
pipelines-backpressure-buffer-ownership.why: Advancing to the wrong position can retain excessive memory, discard unconsumed data, or defeat the backpressure that keeps producers and consumers balanced.
pipelines-backpressure-buffer-ownership.tips: Track consumed and examined positions separately, process ReadOnlySequence segments safely, and complete both ends when ownership ends.

cryptographicoperations-fixed-time-equal.title: Compare authentication values with fixed-time equality
cryptographicoperations-fixed-time-equal.short: Ordinary early-exit equality can leak comparison progress
cryptographicoperations-fixed-time-equal.summary: CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals compares equal-length byte sequences without data-dependent early exit, making it appropriate for MACs and similar secret-derived values.
cryptographicoperations-fixed-time-equal.why: General-purpose sequence equality may stop at the first mismatch and is not designed to provide timing-resistant cryptographic comparison.
cryptographicoperations-fixed-time-equal.tips: Validate lengths and protocol framing separately and use cryptographic primitives rather than inventing a custom constant-time loop.

immutable-collections-snapshot-state.title: Publish immutable collection snapshots for read-heavy shared state
immutable-collections-snapshot-state.short: Readers can share a stable version while writers create the next one
immutable-collections-snapshot-state.summary: Immutable collections let code replace a whole logical snapshot instead of mutating a collection that concurrent readers are traversing.
immutable-collections-snapshot-state.why: This can simplify synchronization for configuration and routing tables, though each update creates structural changes and is not free.
immutable-collections-snapshot-state.tips: Use snapshot replacement when reads dominate and consistency matters; benchmark write-heavy workloads against concurrent or locked mutable structures.

process-async-output-drain.title: Drain redirected process output asynchronously
process-async-output-drain.short: Read stdout and stderr while waiting for process exit
process-async-output-drain.summary: A child process with redirected output should have its output streams consumed while it runs, then be awaited for termination.
process-async-output-drain.why: Waiting for exit before draining bounded OS pipes can deadlock when the child blocks trying to write more output.
process-async-output-drain.tips: Start both output reads before waiting, propagate cancellation deliberately, and define how process termination is handled when cancellation occurs.

ziparchive-stream-lifetime.title: Keep ZipArchive and entry stream lifetimes explicit
ziparchive-stream-lifetime.short: Archive entries depend on their archive and underlying stream
ziparchive-stream-lifetime.summary: ZipArchive entry streams are views over archive data, so their usability and ownership depend on the archive mode, archive lifetime, and leaveOpen choice.
ziparchive-stream-lifetime.why: Returning an entry stream after disposing its archive or accidentally closing a caller-owned base stream creates delayed and confusing failures.
ziparchive-stream-lifetime.tips: Keep archive and entry processing in one ownership scope and use leaveOpen only when another component clearly owns the base stream.

cancellation-registration-lifetime.title: Dispose CancellationToken registrations that have bounded lifetimes
cancellation-registration-lifetime.short: Callbacks can keep state reachable until the token source is released
cancellation-registration-lifetime.summary: CancellationToken.Register returns a registration that can be disposed when a callback is no longer needed.
cancellation-registration-lifetime.why: Long-lived tokens combined with many short-lived registrations can retain callback state and increase cancellation work unnecessarily.
cancellation-registration-lifetime.tips: Dispose registrations at the end of their logical operation and keep cancellation callbacks short, thread-safe, and non-blocking.

aspnet-outputcache-vary-keys.title: Design ASP.NET Core output-cache variation keys deliberately
aspnet-outputcache-vary-keys.short: Cached responses must vary on every request input that changes representation
aspnet-outputcache-vary-keys.summary: ASP.NET Core output caching can reuse generated responses, but the policy must identify query, header, route, or other dimensions that produce distinct content.
aspnet-outputcache-vary-keys.why: An incomplete variation policy can serve the wrong representation, while excessive variation destroys cache effectiveness and can grow key cardinality.
aspnet-outputcache-vary-keys.tips: Cache only suitable endpoints, choose bounded variation dimensions, and exclude personalized or authorization-sensitive output unless the policy proves isolation.

enumerable-trygetnonenumeratedcount.title: Ask for a sequence count without forcing enumeration when possible
enumerable-trygetnonenumeratedcount.short: Some IEnumerable sources already expose their size cheaply
enumerable-trygetnonenumeratedcount.summary: TryGetNonEnumeratedCount can retrieve the size of known collection-like sources without walking the sequence, while still allowing a fallback for general iterators.
enumerable-trygetnonenumeratedcount.why: Calling Count() on an arbitrary iterator may execute the entire pipeline and can repeat expensive or stateful work.
enumerable-trygetnonenumeratedcount.tips: Use this when count is an optimization rather than a requirement; do not assume every IEnumerable can provide a cheap count.

native-library-dllimportresolver.title: Resolve native libraries deliberately for managed interop
native-library-dllimportresolver.short: Map logical P/Invoke library names to platform-specific native binaries
native-library-dllimportresolver.summary: NativeLibrary and DllImportResolver let a managed assembly control how its native dependencies are located and loaded.
native-library-dllimportresolver.why: Cross-platform applications and plugins may need architecture- or platform-specific library selection that default probing cannot express cleanly.
native-library-dllimportresolver.tips: Keep resolution deterministic, validate supported platforms, avoid loading untrusted paths, and preserve safe handle ownership for returned native resources.

unity-profilermarker-hot-paths.title: Add ProfilerMarker scopes around Unity hot paths
unity-profilermarker-hot-paths.short: Measure custom subsystems inside the Unity Profiler
unity-profilermarker-hot-paths.summary: ProfilerMarker adds named timing regions around application code so expensive systems can be separated from broad engine frames during profiling.
unity-profilermarker-hot-paths.why: Optimizing from aggregate frame time alone makes it difficult to identify which custom stage actually regressed.
unity-profilermarker-hot-paths.tips: Mark stable subsystem boundaries rather than every tiny call, profile representative builds, and use measurements to guide allocation and CPU optimization.
